chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no constriction nor expansion except that for Allah in it is will, destiny, and trial.

key_terms.بَسْط: Expansion or ease (in provision, health, or circumstances)
key_terms.قَبْض: Constriction or restriction (in provision, health, or circumstances)

ai.seo_question: What does the concept of qabd and bast mean in Shia theology regarding divine decree?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that both constriction (*qabd*) and expansion (*bast*) are not merely physical states but divine decrees (*qada'*) and wills (*mashiyyah*) intended as trials (*ibtila'*). This underscores the Shia theological view that all circumstances, whether perceived as hardship or ease, are purposeful manifestations of God’s wisdom designed to test the believer’s patience and gratitude.
